scenes.title: Airport Check-in
scenes.zh: 機場報到
scenes.desc: Checking in for the flight to Dublin via Istanbul: passport, bags, seat, and asking about the layover.

lines: Good morning. Where are you flying today?
I'm flying to Dublin via Istanbul. I'd like to check in for my flight, please.
Of course. May I have your passport, please?
Are you traveling for business or vacation?
How many bags would you like to check in today?
I'd like to check one bag.
Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat?
I'd prefer an aisle seat, please. Is the flight full?
It's quite busy today, but there are still a few aisle seats left.
Your bag will be checked through to Dublin, so you don't need to collect it in Istanbul.
Great. How long is the layover in Istanbul?
Do I have enough time to make my connection?
Yes, that should be plenty of time.
Here's your boarding pass. Do you have any other questions?
No, I'm all set. Thank you.

sentences: I'm flying to Dublin via Istanbul.
I'd like to check in for my flight, please.
I'm traveling for vacation.
I'd like to check one bag.
I'd prefer an aisle seat, please.
Is the flight full?
How long is the layover in Istanbul?
Do I have enough time to make my connection?
No, I'm all set. Thank you.
notes: Is the flight full?
Useful when you want an aisle or window seat and aren't sure there are any left.
make my connection
= catch my connecting flight (趕上轉機).

scenes.title: Finding the Gate & Flight Delay
scenes.zh: 找登機門・班機延誤
scenes.desc: Asking the way to Gate A12, checking you're going the right way, and finding out the flight is delayed.

parts.title: Finding the Gate
lines: Hi there. Are you looking for something?
Yes. I've no idea where Gate A12 is. Could you please show me the way?
Sure. Go straight ahead, then take the escalator up to the next floor.
So I go straight and take the escalator up?
Yes, that's right. Then follow the signs for Gate A.
Excuse me, is this the right way to Gate A?
Yes, you're going the right way. Gate A12 is at the end on your left.

parts.title: Flight Delay
lines: Excuse me. My flight is showing as delayed. How long will the flight be delayed?
It looks like the flight will be delayed by about an hour.
Oh no. I've already booked an Aircoach in Dublin. I hope the delay won't mess up my schedule.
What time is your Aircoach booking for?
It's at 10 o'clock on Monday morning.
You should still have enough time. Please keep checking the flight status on the screens.

sentences: I've no idea where Gate A12 is. Could you please show me the way?
So I go straight and take the escalator up?
Is this the right way to Gate A?
How long will the flight be delayed?
I've already booked an Aircoach. I hope the delay won't mess up my schedule.
It's at 10 o'clock on Monday morning.
notes: I've no idea...
Irish/UK casual way to say "I have no idea...".
mess up my schedule
Casual and natural: 打亂我的行程.

scenes.title: Transfer Desk, Boarding Pass & Gate Change
scenes.zh: 轉機櫃台・登機證・換登機門
scenes.desc: In Istanbul: getting the boarding pass for the next flight, asking the walking time, and dealing with a gate change.

parts.title: Transfer Desk
lines: Yes. Is this the right way to Gate 21? I need to connect to Dublin.
Do you already have your boarding pass for Dublin?
No. Where can I get the boarding pass for my next flight?
You can get it at the transfer desk, just over there.
Is there a line for picking up the boarding pass?
If I already have my boarding pass, I won't need to line up, right?
That's right, as long as you don't need anything else from the transfer desk.

parts.title: Walking to the Gate
lines: How long is the walk from here to Gate 21?
It should take about ten minutes.
It's possible, so please keep an eye on the screens.

parts.title: Gate Change
lines: Excuse me, my gate has changed to 27. Where should I go?
Follow the signs to Gate 27. It's about five minutes from here.
But my boarding pass still says Gate 21. Is that OK?
Yes. The information on the airport screens is usually the latest. Your flight number is TK1234, right?
Then Gate 27 is correct. Have a good flight!

sentences: Is this the right way to Gate 21? I need to connect to Dublin.
Where can I get the boarding pass for my next flight?
Is there a line for picking up the boarding pass?
If I already have my boarding pass, I won't need to line up, right?
How long is the walk from here to Gate 21?
Could the gate change?
Excuse me, my gate has changed to 27. Where should I go?
But my boarding pass still says Gate 21. Is that OK?
notes: keep an eye on the screens
= keep checking the screens (隨時留意螢幕).

scenes.title: Security Again, Missed Connection & Baggage
scenes.zh: 再次安檢・錯過轉機・行李
scenes.desc: Finding out you need to go through security again, worrying about missing the connection after a delay, and asking about your checked bag.

lines: Excuse me. I already have my boarding pass for the next flight. Do I still need to go to the transfer desk?
If you already have your boarding pass, you don't need to go to the transfer desk. But you still need to go through security.
You mean I have to go through security once again?
How long does it usually take to go through security?
It depends, but it can take around 15 to 20 minutes.
Oh no. My first flight was delayed. I'm afraid I'll miss my connecting flight.
If you miss your connection because of a delay, please speak to the airline staff at the transfer desk.
Will the airline arrange the next flight for me?
Yes, they should help you arrange another flight.
But how about my baggage? Will it be transferred to the next flight?
If your baggage is checked through to Dublin, it will normally be transferred automatically.
So I don't need to collect my baggage here?
That's right. You don't need to collect it in Istanbul.
So I just go to the new boarding gate, right?
Yes. Please check the airport screens for the latest gate information.

sentences: Do I still need to go to the transfer desk?
You mean I have to go through security once again?
How long does it usually take to go through security?
My first flight was delayed. I'm afraid I'll miss my connecting flight.
If I miss my connecting flight because of a delay, will the airline arrange the next flight for me?
But how about my baggage? Will it be transferred to the next flight?
So I don't need to collect my baggage here?
So I just go to the new boarding gate, right?
notes: I'm afraid I'll...
Use "I'm afraid" to say you're worried something bad will happen (恐怕…).
collect my baggage
More natural than "take my baggage" when you mean picking it up from the airport.

scenes.title: Security Check & Boarding
scenes.zh: 安檢・登機
scenes.desc: Going through security, having your bag checked, finding Gate 27, and boarding.

parts.title: Security
lines: Do you have your boarding pass and passport ready?
Please take your liquids and laptop out of your bag.
Yes, please. Put them in the tray.
Should I take off my coat?
You can keep your shoes on.
Excuse me, could you come over here, please? We need to check your bag.
Do you have any electronics inside?
Yes, I have a camera and a power bank.
Please take them out of your bag. Is this your camera?
That's fine. We'll just have a quick look. OK, you can go.

parts.title: Boarding
lines: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to Gate 27?
Sure. Go straight ahead and follow the signs to Gate 27.

sentences: Yes, here you are.
All the liquids?
How about the laptop?
Should I take off my coat?
How about my shoes?
OK. What's the problem?
Yes, I have a camera and a power bank.
Could you tell me the way to Gate 27?
Is boarding starting now?
Is this line for TK1234?
notes: Could you tell me the way to...?
More natural than "show me the direction to..." when asking for directions.

scenes.title: On Board: Finding Your Seat & Settling In
scenes.zh: 機上：找座位・安頓
scenes.desc: Boarding the aircraft, finding your seat, storing your carry-on bag, asking for a blanket, using the toilet before takeoff, and handling a seat-belt problem.

parts.title: Finding Your Seat
lines: Good evening. Welcome aboard. May I see your boarding pass, please?
Your seat is down the aisle on your left.
Excuse me. This is 18A, a window seat. I thought I booked an aisle seat.
Let me check your boarding pass... Your seat is actually 18C. That's the aisle seat.
Oh, I made a mistake. Sorry!

parts.title: Carry-on Bag & Blanket
lines: May I ask where I can put my carry-on bag?
You can put it in the overhead bin above your seat.
Oh, that one's full. Is it OK if I put my bag in that overhead bin?
Yes, that's fine. You can put it there.
Would you like a pillow or a blanket?

parts.title: Toilet Before Takeoff
lines: Excuse me, can I use the toilet?
Sure, but we're about to close the cabin doors, so please go now. Go straight and turn right.
That's right. It's just ahead on your right.

parts.title: Seat Belt Problem
lines: Excuse me. I can't fasten my seat belt. It seems something is wrong.
Let me have a look. I'm sorry about that. Let me get you another seat.
An aisle seat would be better. Is that OK?
Sure. Let me see if I can find you an aisle seat.
Seat 22C is free. Please follow me.

sentences: I thought I booked an aisle seat.
Oh, I made a mistake. Sorry!
Where can I put my carry-on bag?
Oh, that one's full. Is it OK if I put my bag in that overhead bin?
Blanket, thank you.
Excuse me, can I use the toilet?
Go straight and turn right?
I can't fasten my seat belt. It seems something is wrong.
An aisle seat would be better. Is that OK?
Excuse me. Could you help me with this?
notes: How to get a flight attendant's attention
"Excuse me" is the easiest and safest way. You can also use the call button when appropriate.

scenes.title: On Board: Meals to Landing
scenes.zh: 機上：餐點到降落
scenes.desc: Drinks, snacks and the meal, reclining your seat, the screen and toilet, landing, and getting your bag down.

parts.title: Drinks & Meal
lines: Would you like something to drink?
We have water, orange juice, apple juice, tea, and coffee.
Apple juice, please. Just half a cup.
Would you like something to eat?
Yes, we have some cookies and peanuts.
For dinner, would you like chicken or pasta?
Excuse me, I think my meal isn't warm enough.
I'm sorry about that. Let me see if I can get you another one.
OK, thank you. I appreciate it.
Here you are. Is this one better?
Much better, thank you very much.
Are you finished with your meal?
Excuse me. Could I have some water, please?

parts.title: During the Flight
lines: Yes, that's fine. You can recline your seat now.
Excuse me, there seems to be something wrong with the screen.
I'm afraid it's not working. Would you like me to reset it?
I've reset it for you. It should work now.
Can I use the toilet now?
Yes. The lavatory is just behind you, on your left.

parts.title: Landing
lines: We'll be landing in Dublin in about 30 minutes. Please fasten your seat belts and make sure your seat backs and tray tables are in their upright positions.
Excuse me, could you put your seat back up, please?
Oh, sorry. I'll put my seat back up.
Thank you. Are you all set for landing?
Excuse me, could I get my bag from the overhead bin?

parts.title: Captain's Announcements — Listening Practice
lines: Ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. Welcome aboard.
We'll be cruising at an altitude of 36,000 feet.
Our estimated time of arrival in Dublin is 9:45 a.m.
We may experience some turbulence. Please remain seated with your seat belt fastened.
We have started our descent into Dublin.
We'll be landing in Dublin shortly.
Please fasten your seat belts and return your seat backs to the upright position.
Welcome to Dublin. The local time is 9:40 a.m.
Please remain seated until the seat belt sign has been switched off.

sentences: What do you have?
Apple juice, please. Just half a cup.
Do you have any snacks?
Excuse me, I think my meal isn't warm enough.
OK, thank you. I appreciate it.
Much better, thank you very much.
Yes, I'm done. Thank you.
Could I have some water, please?
Can I recline my seat?
There seems to be something wrong with the screen.
It works, thank you.
Can I use the toilet now?
Is anyone in there?
I'll put my seat back up.
Yes, I'm all set.
Excuse me, could I get my bag from the overhead bin?
notes: toilet / lavatory
toilet 在英國、愛爾蘭最自然；lavatory 是航空用語，比較正式。
Is anyone in there?
Ask this (or knock) when you're not sure if the toilet is free. The sign says "Occupied" or "Vacant".

scenes.title: Immigration at Dublin Airport
scenes.zh: 都柏林入境審查
scenes.desc: Going through immigration after arriving in Dublin.

lines: Good morning. May I see your passport, please?
What's the purpose of your visit?
How long are you staying in Ireland?
I'm staying at the Riverside Hotel, on O'Connell Street.
Do you have a return ticket?
Yes, I do. Here it is.
What do you do for a living?
Have you been to Ireland before?
No, it's my first time in Ireland.
Do you have anything else planned during your stay?
Do you have enough money for your stay?
Yes. I have 500 euros and a credit card.
All right. Everything looks good. Enjoy your stay in Ireland.
Thank you. Have a good day!

sentences: I'm here for a vacation.
I'm staying for 8 days.
I'm staying at the Riverside Hotel, on O'Connell Street.
Yes, I do. Here it is.
I work in an office.
No, it's my first time in Ireland.
I'm traveling alone.
Just some sightseeing.
I have 500 euros and a credit card.
notes: Questions to recognise
What's the purpose of your visit? / How long are you staying in Ireland? / Where are you staying? / Do you have a return ticket?
vacation / holiday
Irish people usually say "I'm here on holiday". "For a vacation" is also understood.

scenes.title: Baggage Reclaim, Delayed Baggage & Customs
scenes.zh: 領行李・行李延誤・海關
scenes.desc: Finding your carousel, someone picking up your bag by mistake, reporting a bag that didn't arrive, and going through customs.

parts.title: Baggage Reclaim
lines: Excuse me, which carousel is the baggage from TK1234 on?
Excuse me, are you waiting for this bag?
Oh, sorry. I think I picked up the wrong bag.

parts.title: If Your Bag Doesn't Arrive
lines: Excuse me, has the carousel stopped? I haven't found my baggage.
Yes, the carousel has stopped. What does your bag look like?
It's black, probably 24 inches. The brand is Departure, and it has a combination lock.
Do you have your baggage tag?
Thank you. I'll check the baggage tracking system for you.
It looks like your bag hasn't arrived yet. It may be on the next flight.
Oh... so when can I get my baggage?
We expect it to arrive on the next flight. We can arrange to have it delivered to your hotel once it arrives.
So, you'll deliver my baggage to my hotel?
Yes. We'll contact you when your bag arrives, and arrange delivery to your hotel.
I can give you my hotel's address. Also, my phone only has internet access, so I can't receive phone calls.
That's fine. We'll send you an email or a text message instead.
OK, I'll give you my email address. Do you know when my baggage will be delivered to my hotel?
It should be delivered by tomorrow.
If I'm out when my baggage arrives, can the hotel receive it for me?
Yes, that's fine. We'll leave it at the front desk.
If I don't get my baggage tomorrow, who should I contact?
You can contact our baggage services team. The contact information is on this form.
OK, I see. Thanks for your help.
You're welcome. I hope you get your bag soon. Have a nice day!

parts.title: Customs
lines: Do you have anything to declare?
No, I don't have anything to declare.
Are you carrying any food, plants, or animal products?
No. I only have some bread from the meal on the plane. Is that OK?
That's fine. You can go through.
Thank you. Have a good day!

sentences: Which carousel is the baggage from TK1234 on?
Excuse me, are you waiting for this bag?
It's OK. It happens sometimes.
Has the carousel stopped? I haven't found my baggage.
It's black, probably 24 inches. The brand is Departure, and it has a combination lock.
When can I get my baggage?
So, you'll deliver my baggage to my hotel?
My phone only has internet access, so I can't receive phone calls.
If I'm out when my baggage arrives, can the hotel receive it for me?
If I don't get my baggage tomorrow, who should I contact?
I don't have anything to declare.
I only have some bread from the meal on the plane. Is that OK?
notes: Order at the airport
Landing → Immigration → Baggage reclaim → Customs. Report a missing bag before you leave the baggage hall.
Questions to recognise
Do you have anything to declare? / What does your bag look like? / It looks like your bag hasn't arrived yet.

scenes.title: Dublin Airport → City Centre
scenes.zh: 機場到市中心・買交通卡
scenes.desc: Finding the Aircoach stop and asking where to get off, then buying a Leap Visitor Card for buses and the Luas.

parts.title: Aircoach
lines: Excuse me, could you help me?
Sure. What can I help you with?
I've booked an Aircoach. Do you know where I can catch it?
Of course. The Aircoach stop is just outside the terminal.
Does it go to the city centre?
How long does it take to get to O'Connell Street?
It usually takes about 30 minutes, depending on traffic.
You should get off at O'Connell Street. The driver will announce it.

parts.title: Transport Pass
lines: Hi. I'm going to be in Dublin for a week. Is there a transport pass that's suitable for tourists?
Yes, there are a few options. What will you mainly be using?
I'll mainly be using buses and the Luas.
In that case, I'd recommend a Leap Visitor Card.
How much is this card? Can I use it for seven days?
The seven-day card costs €40. You can use it on Dublin Bus and the Luas.
So, can I buy it here?
Okay, I'll take one, please. Can I pay by card?
Yes, of course. Just tap your card here.

sentences: I've booked an Aircoach. Do you know where I can catch it?
Does it go to the city centre?
How long does it take to get to O'Connell Street?
Where should I get off?
I'm going to be in Dublin for a week.
Is there a transport pass that's suitable for tourists?
I'll mainly be using buses and the Luas.
How much is this card? Can I use it for seven days?
Can I buy it here?
Okay, I'll take one, please. Can I pay by card?
notes: city centre
Natural Dublin/UK-Irish wording; "downtown" is not the usual choice here.
get to + place
How long does it take to get to O'Connell Street?
catch a bus
"Catch" is the everyday verb for taking a bus, train or the Luas.
the Luas
Use "the" when referring to Dublin's light-rail system.
pay by card / pay with a credit card
Both are natural.

scenes.title: Hotel Check-in & Staying at the Hotel
scenes.zh: 飯店入住
scenes.desc: Checking in, asking about breakfast and room facilities, confirming check-out, leaving luggage after check-out, and finding the lift.

lines: Good afternoon. Welcome to the Riverside Hotel. How can I help you?
Hello. I have a reservation. I'd like to check in.
Certainly. May I have your passport, please?
Thank you. Could you confirm your check-out date for me, please?
Perfect. Here's your key card. You're in Room 214, on the second floor.
Breakfast wasn't included in my reservation. If I want to have breakfast during my stay, how much is it?
Do I need to book it a day in advance?
No, you don't. Just let us know in the morning.
Is there a fridge in the room?
Is there a kettle in the room?
Yes, there's a kettle, along with tea and coffee.
That's good. And what's the Wi-Fi password?
It's written on the key card holder.
May I confirm the check-out time?
Of course. Check-out is at 11 a.m.
Could I leave my luggage here for a while after I check out?
Of course. What time will you be collecting it?
No problem. Just bring it to reception when you check out.
Could you show me where the lift is, please?
Of course. It's just around the corner, next to the stairs.
Yes, that's right. Enjoy your stay!

sentences: I have a reservation. I'd like to check in.
Breakfast wasn't included in my reservation.
If I want to have breakfast during my stay, how much is it?
Do I need to book it a day in advance?
Is there a fridge in the room?
Is there a kettle in the room?
What's the Wi-Fi password?
May I confirm the check-out time?
Could I leave my luggage here for a while after I check out?
Could you show me where the lift is, please?
This way, right?
notes: Floors in Ireland
Ground floor = 1 樓, first floor = 2 樓, second floor = 3 樓.
Baggage vs. Luggage
Both mean the bags you travel with. Baggage is common in airline expressions (checked baggage, baggage reclaim); luggage is common for travel bags (my luggage, luggage storage).

scenes.title: Hotel Problems: Bathroom Light & Key Card
scenes.zh: 飯店問題：浴室燈・房卡
scenes.desc: Calling reception about a flickering bathroom light, and later finding that your key card doesn't work.

parts.title: Bathroom Light
lines: Good evening. Reception. How can I help you?
Hi, I'm calling from Room 214. There's something wrong with the light in the bathroom.
I'm sorry to hear that. What seems to be the problem with the light?
I'll send someone up to take a look at it.
Okay, thank you. How long will it take?
Someone should be up in about 10 minutes.
Okay, I'll wait in the room.
Hello, maintenance. I'm here about the bathroom light.
Hi, please come in. It's this one.
It looks like the bulb needs to be replaced. I'll replace it for you.
There you go. It should be working properly now.
Great, it's working now. Thank you for your help.

parts.title: Key Card
lines: Good evening. How can I help you?
Hi, my key card isn't working. I can't get into my room.
Could I have your room number, please?
It looks like your key card has expired. I'll reprogram it for you.
Here you go. Could you try it again?
Okay, I'll go upstairs and try it.

sentences: I'm calling from Room 214.
There's something wrong with the light in the bathroom.
The light keeps flickering.
How long will it take?
I'll wait in the room.
Hi, please come in. It's this one.
Great, it's working now. Thank you for your help.
My key card isn't working.
I can't get into my room.
Two one four.
I'll go upstairs and try it.
Great! It works!
notes: I'm calling from Room 214.
Natural when calling reception from your room.
There's something wrong with...
Useful for reporting a problem.
The light keeps flickering.
keep + V-ing means something continues to happen.
Two one four.
Say room numbers digit by digit. 0 is often said "oh" (305 = three oh five).
upstairs
One word: go upstairs.

scenes.title: Hotel: Heating & TV
scenes.zh: 飯店：暖氣・電視
scenes.desc: Calling reception because the room is cold and you can't work the heater, then asking about the TV remote, Netflix and AirPlay.

parts.title: Heating
lines: Hello, I'm calling from Room 214. It's a little cold, and I don't know how to adjust the heater.
No problem. There should be a control panel on the wall. Have you tried using it?
Yes, I've tried, but I still don't know how to use it.
Okay. First, press the power button. Then set the temperature to around 20 degrees.
Okay. Do I need to leave it on all the time?
No, you don't. You can turn it off when you go out.
Okay, I got it. Thanks for explaining.
You're welcome. Just let us know if you have any other problems.

parts.title: TV
lines: Actually, I have one more question. How do I use the TV remote? I always have trouble using hotel remotes.
Of course. Press the red button at the top to turn the TV on, and use the buttons marked CH to change the channels.
How do I adjust the volume?
Does the TV have Netflix or Disney+?
It has Netflix, but not Disney+. You'll need to sign in with your own account.
And can I use AirPlay on the TV?
That's okay. I just wanted to make sure. Thank you.
You're very welcome. Have a good evening!

sentences: It's a little cold, and I don't know how to adjust the heater.
I've tried, but I still don't know how to use it.
Do I need to leave it on all the time?
Okay, I got it. Thanks for explaining.
Actually, I have one more question.
How do I use the TV remote?
I always have trouble using hotel remotes.
How do I adjust the volume?
Does the TV have Netflix or Disney+?
Can I use AirPlay on the TV?
That's okay. I just wanted to make sure.
notes: adjust the heater
Use this when you don't know how to change the heating settings.
leave it on
Means keep it switched on.
Thanks for explaining.
Natural for thanking someone for an explanation.
Actually, I have one more question.
A natural way to add another question before the call ends.
TV remote
Much more natural than "television remote controller".
have trouble + V-ing
Useful for saying you have difficulty doing something.

scenes.title: Hotel Housekeeping & Extra Supplies
scenes.zh: 飯店：打掃房間・加備品
scenes.desc: Asking housekeeping to make up the room while you go out, then requesting fresh towels, hangers and toilet paper.

parts.title: Making Up the Room
lines: Good morning. Reception. How can I help you?
Good morning. I'm calling from Room 214. Could you please make up my room today?
Of course. What time would you like us to make up your room?
Do I need to leave the room?
No, you don't. You can stay in the room if you like, but we'll need some space to clean.
Okay, I think I'll go out for a while.
Should I remove the "Do Not Disturb" sign so you can come in?
Yes, please. That way, housekeeping will know they can come in and clean your room.
Okay. Then I'll be back around 3 p.m.
Perfect. Your room will be ready when you get back. Enjoy your afternoon!

parts.title: Fresh Towels & Extra Supplies
lines: Hello, I'm calling from Room 214. It seems that housekeeping didn't leave any fresh towels.
I'm sorry about that. How many towels do you need?
One bath towel and two hand towels, please.
Of course. We'll bring them up to your room shortly.
Could I also have two more hangers, please?
Of course. We'll bring two more hangers up with the towels.
Oh, and could you also bring me a roll of toilet paper, please?
No problem. Towels, hangers and a roll of toilet paper. Anything else?

sentences: Could you please make up my room today?
Is 2 p.m. okay?
Do I need to leave the room?
I think I'll go out for a while.
Should I remove the "Do Not Disturb" sign so you can come in?
Then I'll be back around 3 p.m.
It seems that housekeeping didn't leave any fresh towels.
One bath towel and two hand towels, please.
Could I also have two more hangers, please?
Could you also bring me a roll of toilet paper, please?
No, that's all. Thank you!
notes: make up the room
Hotel phrase for cleaning and tidying a guest room.
It seems that...
A soft, polite way to point out a problem without sounding like a complaint.

scenes.title: Hotel Breakfast & Local Breakfast Recommendations
scenes.zh: 飯店早餐・推薦愛爾蘭早餐
scenes.desc: Deciding to have breakfast at the hotel one morning, then asking the receptionist for a good Irish breakfast place nearby.

parts.title: Having Breakfast at the Hotel
lines: Good morning. How can I help you?
Good morning. I'd like to have breakfast here this morning. Is that possible?
Yes, of course. It's €15 per person.
You can pay now, or you can charge it to your room.
Okay, please charge it to my room.
Certainly. Breakfast is in the dining room on the first floor.
What time is breakfast served until?
Okay, I'll go now. Thank you!

parts.title: In the Dining Room
lines: Good morning! What's your room number, please?
Thank you. Please take a seat anywhere you'd like.
Excuse me, where can I get coffee and tea?
The coffee and tea are over there, next to the juice.
Can I help myself to the juice?
Which one is the orange juice?
The one on the left is orange juice.
Excuse me, could I have a butter knife, please?
Of course. I'll get one for you.
May I take some fruit back to my room?
I'm afraid not. The food and drinks are only for the dining room.
You're welcome. Enjoy the rest of your breakfast!

parts.title: Asking for a Nearby Irish Breakfast
lines: Could you recommend a good Irish breakfast place nearby?
Certainly. There's a lovely café about a five-minute walk from here. Would you like me to show you on the map?
Here it is. It's just around the corner.
Do I need to book in advance?
No, you don't. You can just walk in, but it can get quite busy on weekends.
I'd recommend going around 9 a.m. It's usually quieter then.
Okay. I'll go around 9 a.m. tomorrow. Thanks for the recommendation.
You're very welcome. I hope you enjoy it!

sentences: I'd like to have breakfast here this morning. Is that possible?
So, do I pay now?
Please charge it to my room.
What time is breakfast served until?
Excuse me, where can I get coffee and tea?
Can I help myself to the juice?
Which one is the orange juice?
Could I have a butter knife, please?
May I take some fruit back to my room?
Could you recommend a good Irish breakfast place nearby?
Do I need to book in advance?
What time would you recommend?
Thanks for the recommendation.
notes: Please charge it to my room.
A natural way to add a hotel expense to your room bill and pay at check-out.
What time is breakfast served until?
A natural way to ask when breakfast ends.
Can I help myself to the juice?
help yourself to... means take something yourself.
Do I need to book in advance?
A useful general question for restaurants, attractions, and activities.

scenes.title: Restaurant — Dinner, Dessert & Card Payment Problem
scenes.zh: 餐廳：晚餐・甜點・刷卡失敗
scenes.desc: Getting a table, ordering dinner, taking leftovers to go, ordering dessert, asking about tipping, and dealing with a card that doesn't work.

parts.title: Getting a Table & Ordering
lines: Good evening! Do you have a reservation?
No, I don't. Do you have a table for one?
May I have a window seat?
Certainly. Right this way. Here's the menu. Is this your first time here?
Yes, it is. What would you recommend?
Our seafood pasta is very popular.
Is it too much for one person?
It's a fairly generous portion, but it should be fine for one person.
Okay, I'll have the seafood pasta, please.
Do I have to order a drink, or could I just have some water?
Water is fine. Still or sparkling?

parts.title: Leftovers & Dessert
lines: Excuse me. I can't finish this. Could I get it to go, please?
Of course. I'll bring you a takeaway box.
And could I see the dessert menu?
Certainly. Here you are. Our chocolate brownie is very popular.
Let me see... Does the brownie come with ice cream?
Yes, it comes with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Would you like to try it?

parts.title: The Bill & Card Problem
lines: Excuse me, could I have the bill, please?
Is service included? Do I need to pay a tip?
No, there's no service charge included. Tipping is optional.
Okay, thank you. I'd like to pay by card. Here you are.
I'm sorry, but your card was declined.
Oops... Could you try this one, please?
I'm afraid this one isn't working either.
What happened? Is there a problem with the card machine?
It seems to be working for other payments. Would you like me to try your card again?
Yes, could you please try again?
I'm sorry, it still isn't going through.
I'm sorry. My cards usually work fine. What should I do?
Let me speak to my manager and see what we can do.
We can make an exception this time. If you have some cash for part of the bill, we can work something out.
Really? I really appreciate that. I'll go back to my hotel and try to set up Apple Pay. Then I'll come back later. Is that okay?
Yes, that's absolutely fine. I'll make a note of it. Just come back when you can.
Thank you so much for understanding. I'll be back soon.
No problem at all. Have a good night!

sentences: Do you have a table for one?
May I have a window seat?
What would you recommend?
Is it too much for one person?
Do I have to order a drink, or could I just have some water?
I can't finish this. Could I get it to go, please?
Could I see the dessert menu?
Does the brownie come with ice cream?
Could I have the bill, please?
Is service included? Do I need to pay a tip?
I'd like to pay by card.
Could you try this one, please?
Is there a problem with the card machine?
My cards usually work fine. What should I do?
I'll go back to my hotel and try to set up Apple Pay. Then I'll come back later. Is that okay?
Thank you so much for understanding.
notes: Could I get it to go?
A natural way to ask for takeaway in a restaurant.
Is service included?
Ask this when you're not sure if the bill already includes a service charge.
It isn't going through.
Means the card payment hasn't been accepted.

scenes.title: Café — Tea, Cake, Water & Toilet
scenes.zh: 咖啡店：茶・蛋糕・水・廁所
scenes.desc: Ordering a hot peppermint tea with no sugar, choosing a cake, asking for water, and using the toilet.

lines: Good morning! What can I get for you?
Let me see... Do you have any decaf options?
Sure. We have decaf coffee, tea, and hot chocolate. Would you like something hot or cold?
Something hot. Do you have any herbal tea?
Yes, we do. We have peppermint tea and chamomile tea. Which one would you like?
A hot peppermint tea, and no sugar, please.
Sure. One hot peppermint tea, no sugar.
Yes, we have chocolate cake, carrot cake, and cheesecake today.
I'd recommend the carrot cake. It's one of our most popular ones.
Oh, I don't like carrots. Haha. I'll have the chocolate cake, please.
No worries at all! Chocolate cake it is. Anything else?
Of course. Would you like still or sparkling water?
Sure. I'll bring you a glass of still water.
And may I use the toilet?
Of course. It's just at the back, on your left.

sentences: May I see the menu?
Do you have any decaf options?
Do you have any herbal tea?
A hot peppermint tea, and no sugar, please.
Do you have any cakes?
What do you recommend?
I don't like carrots. I'll have the chocolate cake, please.
May I have some water?
Still, please.
May I use the toilet?
notes: No worries at all!
A friendly Irish/UK way of saying "no problem".
... it is.
"Chocolate cake it is" = OK, chocolate cake then (確認你的選擇).

scenes.title: Clothes Shop — Trying On & Buying a Jacket
scenes.zh: 服飾店：試穿・買外套
scenes.desc: Browsing, asking for a size, trying on a jacket that doesn't suit you, finding another one on sale, and paying by card.

parts.title: Browsing
lines: Hi! Can I help you with anything?
Excuse me, do you have this in a medium?
Let me check for you. Yes, we do. Here's a medium. Would you like to try it on?
Hmm... I don't think it suits me. Sorry.
No problem at all. Would you like to try something else?
No, thank you. I'll have another look around.
Of course. Just let me know if you need any help.

parts.title: Buying a Jacket
lines: Excuse me, how much is this jacket?
It is a little pricey, but it's currently 20% off.
How much is it after the 20% discount?
Of course. The fitting rooms are just over there.
It fits well. I like it.
Great! Would you like to take it?
Hmm... let me think about it.
Sure, no problem. Take your time.
Great! How would you like to pay?
Sure. That'll be €71.99, please. You can tap your card here.
No, you don't. Here's your receipt and your bag. Have a nice day!
Thank you. Have a nice day!

sentences: Just looking around, thanks.
Do you have this in a medium?
I don't think it suits me. Sorry.
I'll have another look around.
How much is this jacket?
That's a bit expensive.
How much is it after the 20% discount?
May I try it on?
It fits well. I like it.
Let me think about it.
Okay, I'll take it.
By card, please.
Do I need to sign?
notes: suit vs. fit
It suits me = 好看、適合我；It fits = 尺寸剛好。
20% off
Means the price is reduced by 20% (= 八折).

scenes.title: Supermarket — Finding Items & Choosing Snacks
scenes.zh: 超市：找商品・選零食
scenes.desc: Finding bottled water, asking about popular Irish snacks, choosing a flavour, and finding individual yogurts.

lines: Excuse me, could you tell me where the bottled water is?
Sure. It's in aisle five, near the soft drinks.
Where can I find aisle five?
It's just over there, on your right, next to aisle four.
Thank you. Also, what's a popular snack in Ireland?
Tayto crisps are very popular in Ireland. You should give them a try!
Which flavour is the most popular?
I'd say cheese and onion is probably the most popular.
Great. Is there anything else you're looking for?
Yogurt... Can you show me where I can find it?
Sure. The yogurt is in the refrigerated section, just past the milk.
Do you have any single packs?
Yes, we do. The individual ones are on the top shelf, next to the larger packs.
I'd recommend the Greek yogurt. It's really popular.

sentences: Excuse me, could you tell me where the bottled water is?
Where can I find aisle five?
What's a popular snack in Ireland?
Which flavour is the most popular?
Can you show me where I can find it?
Do you have any single packs?
Which one would you recommend?
notes: crisps
In Ireland and the UK, "crisps" are potato chips. "Chips" are hot fries.
Tayto
A classic Irish crisp brand. Cheese & onion is the famous flavour.

scenes.title: Supermarket Checkout — Paying by Card & Using Your Own Bag
scenes.zh: 超市結帳：刷卡・自備購物袋
scenes.desc: Checking out, paying by card, and telling the cashier that you brought your own shopping bag.

lines: Hi. Did you find everything you were looking for?
Yes, thank you. I found everything I was looking for.
Great. Do you need a bag?
No, thanks. I don't need a plastic bag. I have my own shopping bag.
No problem. Your total is €18.65. How would you like to pay?
Sure. Just tap your card here.
Here's your receipt. Have a nice day!

sentences: Yes, thank you. I found everything I was looking for.
No, thanks. I don't need a plastic bag.
I have my own shopping bag.
By card, please.
Thank you. You too!
notes: Bags in Ireland
Shops charge for plastic bags, so cashiers often ask "Do you need a bag?".

scenes.title: Supermarket — Asking for a Refund
scenes.zh: 超市：要求退款
scenes.desc: Returning to the supermarket after finding oranges cheaper at a stall outside. The store first says no, then makes an exception.

lines: Hi there. How can I help you?
I bought these oranges here just a few minutes ago. Could I get a refund?
Of course. Is there a problem with the oranges?
No, there's nothing wrong with the oranges. I just found some cheaper ones at a stall outside.
I see. Do you still have the receipt?
Thank you. Hmm, I'm afraid we can't offer a refund just because you found them cheaper somewhere else. Our refund policy only covers faulty or damaged products.
Oh... really? Then, can I exchange them for something else?
Unfortunately, we can't exchange them either, because they're not faulty.
Okay, I see. It's okay. Thank you.
Wait a moment. Let me check with my manager.
Okay, we can make an exception this time. We can give you a refund.
Oh, really? Thank you so much!
No problem. I'll put the refund back on your card. Is that okay? It should appear in your account within a few days.
Thanks for your help. Have a nice day!

sentences: I bought these oranges here just a few minutes ago. Could I get a refund?
There's nothing wrong with the oranges. I just found some cheaper ones at a stall outside.
Can I exchange them for something else?
Okay, I see. It's okay. Thank you.
Oh, really? Thank you so much!
Thanks for your help. Have a nice day!
notes: I'm afraid we can't...
A polite way staff say no. Listen for "I'm afraid" — it usually means bad news.

scenes.title: Fruit Stall — Buying Strawberries & Oranges
scenes.zh: 水果攤：買草莓・柳橙
scenes.desc: Buying a small amount of fruit, asking for a plastic bag, and paying with a €10 note.

lines: Hi there! What can I get for you?
They're €5 a punnet. Would you like one?
That's a bit too much for me. I'm traveling alone. Could I just get half a punnet?
Sure, no problem. Half a punnet is €2.50.
And the oranges are €2 for 10? Can I buy five?
Yes, that's right. Five for €1. Would you like to choose them yourself?
Yes, please. May I have a plastic bag?
Of course. Here you are. Anything else?
That's all. How much is it altogether?
Sorry, I don't have a smaller note. Here's €10.
Thank you! Have a good day!

sentences: How much are these strawberries?
That's a bit too much for me.
Could I just get half a punnet?
The oranges are €2 for 10? Can I buy five?
May I have a plastic bag?
That's all. How much is it altogether?
Sorry, I don't have a smaller note.
notes: punnet
Irish/UK word for the small box that berries are sold in.
note
In Ireland/UK, paper money is a "note" (not a "bill").

scenes.title: Street Food Stall — Smoked Salmon Sandwich Meal
scenes.zh: 街頭小吃：煙燻鮭魚三明治套餐
scenes.desc: Ordering a sandwich meal deal, asking about drinks and crisp flavours, paying by card, and asking to have the sandwich cut in half.

lines: Hi there! What can I get for you?
I'd like a smoked salmon sandwich.
Sure. Would you like anything else with that? We have crisps, salad, and drinks.
Do you have a meal deal, or do I have to order everything separately?
Yes, we have a meal deal. You can get a sandwich, a bag of crisps, and a drink for €8.50.
Okay. Then I'd like the smoked salmon sandwich meal, please.
Sure. What would you like to drink? We have still water, sparkling water, and soft drinks.
What kind of soft drinks do you have?
We have Coca-Cola, Diet Coke, Sprite, and Fanta.
And which crisps would you like? We have salt & vinegar, cheese & onion, and ready salted.
It's a little tangy and sour. If you don't like sour flavours, I'd recommend the ready salted.
One smoked salmon sandwich meal with Sprite and ready salted crisps. That'll be €8.50, please.
Yes, of course. Just tap your card here.
Yes, that's gone through. You're all set.
Excuse me, could you cut my sandwich in half, please?
Of course. No problem. Here you are. Enjoy!

sentences: I'd like a smoked salmon sandwich.
Do you have a meal deal, or do I have to order everything separately?
What kind of soft drinks do you have?
What's salt & vinegar like?
Ready salted, please.
Can I pay by card?
Is that okay?
Could you cut my sandwich in half, please?
notes: meal deal
Very common in Ireland/UK: a sandwich + snack + drink for one price.
What's ... like?
Ask this when you want someone to describe a taste or thing.
That's gone through.
The card payment was successful.

scenes.title: Market — Browsing, Asking for a Discount & Coming Back to Buy
scenes.zh: 市集：逛逛・殺價・回頭買
scenes.desc: Looking at a handmade item, asking for a discount, thinking about it, then returning later to buy it.

parts.title: First Visit
lines: Hi there! Feel free to have a look around.
Can I pick it up and have a look?
Of course! Go ahead. It's handmade locally.
It's really pretty, but... is there any chance you could give me a little discount?
Hmm... I could give you 10% off. Would that help?
Hmm... I'll think about it. Thank you!

parts.title: Coming Back
lines: Hi, I'm back. You said 10% off, right?
Yes, that's right. Would you like to go ahead with it?
Great! That'll be €13.50 with the discount. Card or cash?
Sure. Just tap your card here.
Perfect. Here's your item. Thank you!

sentences: How much is this one?
Can I pick it up and have a look?
It's really pretty, but... is there any chance you could give me a little discount?
I'll think about it. Thank you!
Hi, I'm back. You said 10% off, right?
Okay, I'll take it!
Card, please.
There you go.
notes: Is there any chance you could...?
A soft, polite way to ask for something like a discount.

scenes.title: Visiting The Ramparts Practice Location
scenes.zh: 拜訪 The Ramparts 練唱地點
scenes.desc: You visit a place where the choir sometimes practises. You ask whether you can see the practice room, listen from the stairs if they are rehearsing, and take a few photos if the room is empty.

lines: Hi there. Can I help you?
Hi, does the Ramparts Choir sometimes practice here?
Yes, they do. They usually practice here once or twice a week.
Would it be possible to have a look at where they practice?
Sure. If you'd like, I can show you the room. It's just down the hallway.
If they're practicing right now, you can listen from the stairs, as long as you don't go into the room.
Would it be okay if I just listened from the stairs for a little while?

parts.title: If No One Is Using the Room
lines: If no one's using the room, would it be okay if I took a few photos?
Yes, that's fine. You can take a few photos, but please don't take photos of anyone without asking.
You're very welcome. I hope you enjoy your visit!

sentences: Does the Ramparts Choir sometimes practice here?
Would it be possible to have a look at where they practice?
Would it be okay if I just listened from the stairs for a little while?
If no one's using the room, would it be okay if I took a few photos?
notes: Would it be possible to...?
A polite way to ask whether something is allowed or possible.
Would it be okay if I...?
A natural way to ask for permission before doing something.
listen from the stairs
Natural when you want to listen without entering the room.
if no one's using the room
Natural conversational wording for "if the room is empty".
take a few photos
More natural here than simply "take photos", because you are asking to take only a small number.
Please don't take photos of anyone without asking.
A useful permission/safety phrase to understand.

scenes.title: Unexpectedly Meeting a Member of The Ramparts
scenes.zh: 巧遇 The Ramparts 團員
scenes.desc: A personal conversation for the possibility of meeting a member of The Ramparts in Dublin, after discovering their 10th Anniversary Concert falls on your final night in Dublin.

lines: Excuse me. Are you Kevin from The Ramparts?
Wow! I recognize you from the TV show My Name Is Gabriel. I'm a fan of Bogum's, and I'm from Taiwan. It's nice to meet you!
Oh, really? Thank you! Nice to meet you. Are you here on holiday?
Yes. I'm staying here for eight days. And I'm so lucky that your 10th Anniversary Concert happens to be on my last night in Dublin, so I booked a ticket!
Oh, that's great! So you came to Dublin because of the show?
Yes, I'm here because of Bogum. Haha! And I really love your a cappella singing.
Thank you! That's lovely to hear.
I was really touched by how kind you guys were to him at the time. This might sound a little strange, but I also want to say thank you for being so kind to Bogum.
Oh, thank you! That's really sweet of you to say. We really enjoyed having him with us. Have you been to any of the places where we filmed?
Yes! I've actually been to the house he stayed in, Angel Coffee, where he first met the four members, and the community centre where you practiced singing together.
Wow, you really did your homework! Did you enjoy visiting those places?
Yes, I really like Dublin. And I really loved seeing Bogum with you guys on My Name Is Gabriel. It was really special.
That's so nice. Thanks for coming all this way!
I won't keep you. It was really nice meeting you. Thank you so much! See you at the concert!

sentences: Excuse me. Are you Kevin from The Ramparts?
I recognize you from the TV show My Name Is Gabriel.
I'm a fan of Bogum's.
I'm staying here for eight days.
I'm so lucky that your 10th Anniversary Concert happens to be on my last night in Dublin.
I'm here because of Bogum.
I really love your a cappella singing.
I was really touched by how kind you guys were to him at the time.
This might sound a little strange, but I also want to say thank you for being so kind to Bogum.
I've actually been to the house he stayed in.
I really loved seeing Bogum with you guys on My Name Is Gabriel.
I won't keep you.
It was really nice meeting you. Thank you so much!
notes: Are you Kevin from The Ramparts?
Natural and friendly when confirming someone's identity in this context.
I'm a fan of Bogum's.
Natural spoken English for saying you are Bogum's fan.
I'm here because of Bogum.
Use because of + noun when giving the reason you came.
a cappella
The standard spelling for singing without instrumental accompaniment.
I was really touched by how kind you guys were to him.
A natural way to express that their kindness emotionally affected you.
This might sound a little strange, but...
A gentle way to introduce something personal when you are worried it may feel unexpected.
thank you for being so kind to Bogum
More natural in conversation than the formal "thank you for your kindness to Bogum".
the house he stayed in
Keep "in" because we say stay in a house/place.
I won't keep you.
A natural way to end the conversation politely when you don't want to take up more of their time.
